      "text": "If you are suspended again before your violation record clears in 2028, it will likely result in a **permanent ban**.       "text": "If a server owner is permanently banned and their account is eventually deleted, **the server itself does not automatically get deleted**. It will remain online and fully functional for all the remaining members. \n\nHowever, the \"Deleted User\" will technically remain the owner of the server, which creates major problems for managing it long-term (e.g., you cannot delete the server, manage certain integrations, or assign new top-level roles). \n\nHere is exactly what happens to those servers and how the community can handle it:\n\n### 1. Transferring Ownership (The 100+ Member Rule)\nDiscord Support can manually step in and transfer ownership to another member, but the server and the person requesting it must meet strict criteria:\n*   The server must have **at least 100 members**.\n*   The person requesting ownership must already have **Administrator** or **Moderator** permissions.\n*   The remaining staff must wait **at least 30 days** after the owner was banned (Discord requires the owner\u0027s account to be fully inactive for a month before they intervene).\n*   The server cannot be monetized.\n\n### 2. The Catch: Discord Can Deny It\nThere is a major caveat. Discord\u0027s official policy states that if the original owner was permanently disabled for Terms of Service violations, **Support reserves the right to deny the transfer request**. Because your specific violation is \"platform manipulation,\" Discord might refuse to hand the server over to someone else if they suspect the server itself was involved in the rule-breaking. \n\n### 3. What about small servers (under 100 members)?\nIf the server has fewer than 100 members, Discord Support will completely refuse to transfer ownership—no exceptions. The \"Deleted User\" will own it forever.\n\n**What the remaining members should do:**\nIf a community finds themselves in a server owned by a banned user, and they cannot get Discord to transfer ownership, the official recommendation from Discord Support is to **create a brand new server**. Since the old server is still active, the remaining admins should set up a new server, mass-ping the old server with an invite link, and migrate the community over.",

      "finishReason": "STOP",
      "tokenCount": 590,
      "parts": [{
        "text": "If a server owner"
      }, {
        "text": " is permanently banned and their account is eventually deleted, **the server itself does not automatically get deleted**"
      }, {
        "text": ". It will remain online and fully functional for all the remaining members. \n\nHowever"
      }, {
        "text": ", the \"Deleted User\" will technically remain the owner of the server"
      }, {
        "text": ", which creates major problems for managing it long-term (e.g., you cannot delete the server, manage certain"
      }, {
        "text": " integrations, or assign new top-level roles). \n\nHere is exactly what happens to those servers and how the community can handle"
      }, {
        "text": " it:\n\n### 1. Transferring Ownership (The 100+ Member Rule)\nDiscord Support can manually step in and"
      }, {
        "text": " transfer ownership to another member, but the server and the person requesting it must meet strict criteria"
      }, {
        "text": ":\n*   The server must have **at least 100 members**.\n*   "
      }, {
        "text": "The person requesting ownership must already have **Administrator** or **Moderator** permissions.\n"
      }, {
        "text": "*   The remaining staff must wait **at least 30 days** after the owner was banned (Discord requires the owner\u0027"
      }, {
        "text": "s account to be fully inactive for a month before they intervene).\n*   The server cannot be"
      }, {
        "text": " monetized.\n\n### 2. The Catch: Discord Can Deny It\nThere"
      }, {
        "text": " is a major caveat. Discord\u0027s official policy states that if the original owner was permanently disabled for Terms of Service violations, **Support"
      }, {
        "text": " reserves the right to deny the transfer request**. Because"
      }, {
        "text": " your specific violation is \"platform manipulation,\" Discord might refuse to hand the server over to someone else if they suspect the server"
      }, {
        "text": " itself was involved in the rule-breaking. \n\n"
      }, {
        "text": "### 3. What about small servers (under 100 members)?\nIf the server has fewer than "
      }, {
        "text": "100 members, Discord Support will completely refuse to transfer ownership—no exceptions"
      }, {
        "text": ". The \"Deleted User\" will own it forever"
      }, {
        "text": ".\n\n**What the remaining members should do:**\nIf a community finds themselves in a server owned by a"
      }, {
        "text": " banned user, and they cannot get Discord to transfer ownership, the official recommendation from Discord Support is to **create a brand"
      }, {
        "text": " new server**. Since the old server is still active"
      }, {
        "text": ", the remaining admins should set up a new server, mass-ping the old server with an invite link, and migrate"
      }, {
        "text": " the community over."
      }, {
